S: SRP-1: A class or module carries more than one reason to change (multiple unrelated responsibilities / god object).
SRP-2: A function interleaves multiple levels of abstraction (high-level orchestration mixed with low-level detail in one body).
SRP-3: A change to one feature forces edits to code that serves an unrelated feature in the same unit.
O: OCP-1: Behavior is extended by editing existing code via an if/elif or match on a type tag, instead of adding a new subtype/strategy.
OCP-2: Adding a new variant requires modifying a closed conditional rather than registering a new implementation.
L: LSP-1: A subclass strengthens a precondition or weakens a postcondition of the base method it overrides.
LSP-2: An override raises NotImplementedError or changes the base contract (return type or raised exceptions) so the subtype is not substitutable.
LSP-3: A subclass overrides a method to do nothing or to reject inputs the base accepts.
I: ISP-1: An interface or abstract base forces implementers to define methods they do not use (fat interface).
ISP-2: A client depends on a broad interface but calls only a small subset of its methods.
D: DIP-1: A high-level module directly instantiates a concrete low-level dependency (hard-coded construction, no injection).
DIP-2: Code depends on a concrete class where it should depend on an abstraction or protocol.
DIP-3: A policy/business-logic unit imports and calls a specific I/O, database, or network implementation directly.
